summary.qualitative: Structurally the candidate is compliant — five labeled sections in order, each D item tagged with an origin, no stray commentary — but substantively it captures only the last two turns of a nine-turn session and almost nothing verifiable. Entire workstreams vanish: the ~/.claude-home zsh wrapper that actually resolved task 2, the whole TypeSafe skill summary, the jev-distill-routing repo, and every number the session produced (v1.1.17, 65 SPINE entries, 22,585 rubric chars, $0.50 cap blowout, $1.72 spend, 2.7s median choose, 4/4 hit rate, 41% never distilled, $0.002/session). Worse, it asserts the routing baseline as a future step when it had already run, and it invents rationales for two D-section decisions (the exchanges unit and the separate repo) while crediting the assistant's arithmetic to the user. Its genuine strengths are narrow: the cold-read pivot, the exchanges concept, Jev pricing, ground-truth need, and the recall-over-precision policy are all correctly reported — but section A is largely a vague paraphrase of failures whose diagnostic detail is the reference's main value, and section C is generic praise that would fit almost any session.

candidate_claims.note: Binary string 'for security home-directory trust is never saved' / 'home trust is session-only'.
Wrong actor: the tool harness notified the assistant, not the user; the user was never involved in this.
candidate_claims.reason: The background-task notification is real; its recipient is wrong — the harness notified the assistant, not the user.

candidate_claims.note: cut illegal byte sequence and ugrep complexity-limit errors.
Both Python passes failed — one produced no output, the other garbled minified text; the conclusion came from the earlier strings|grep literals, and no code was located.
candidate_claims.reason: The follow-up Python scripts genuinely ran; their outcome is wrong — both failed and no code was located.

candidate_claims.note: This was a previously recorded 'marks' case (2026-08-02) in projects/aura-distill.md, not an attempt in this session; and the reason was that the conversation is already in warm context, not that the process is costly.
candidate_claims.reason: The 'marks' case is real in projects/aura-distill.md; the claim mis-places it in this session and swaps its reason (warm context, not process cost).

candidate_claims.note: The assistant produced all of that arithmetic; the user's input was qualitative ('gains are not that crazy'). 'Number of signals' data never existed in the session.
candidate_claims.reason: The transcript-volume and cost data are real but were produced by the assistant; 'number of signals' data additionally never existed.

candidate_claims.note: Clearly true of turn 8; 'frequently' is a mild over-generalization across a mostly terse session.
Over-claimed: the user only ever said 'go' once; the final pre-filter proposal was never responded to — the session ended awaiting his decision.
candidate_claims.reason: The user's single 'go' and his engagement with the pivot are real; 'readily accepted suggestions and incorporated new ideas' over-claims their strength.

candidate_claims.note: The user's opening directives were an install status check, the trust prompt, and a TypeSafe summary; the first Jev directive was a routing benchmark, not '/distill improvement'.
candidate_claims.reason: Real user directives exist, but the first Jev directive was a SPINE routing benchmark; '/distill improvement' mis-states the actual instruction.

candidate_claims.note: The 59%/41% figure came from projects/aura-distill.md knowledge, not the ledger; the ledger was proposed as the future ground-truth source. Also drops the 41% number.
candidate_claims.reason: The never-processed-sessions target and the 59%/41% split are real; the source is wrong (project knowledge, not the ledger) and the 41% figure is dropped.

candidate_claims.note: Rationale correct; the 'Convention' origin label is questionable — the transcript derives it from cost evidence and a stated principle.
The actual reasoning was that transcripts are ~90% tool I/O and signals anchor on user text, giving a ~10x code-only cut; the exchange unit was chosen to answer the cross-block worry.
candidate_claims.reason: The exchange-unit decision and its reasoning are real (~90% tool I/O, signals anchor on user text, ~10x cut); the stated driver is a mis-rendering of it.

candidate_claims.note: Rationale invented — the transcript says it is 'a different question than routing' and 'both are small'; and it was a proposal pending user approval, not a decision.
candidate_claims.reason: The repo-split proposal is real; the stated rationale (isolate functionality, avoid dependencies) replaces the actual one and 'was chosen' over-states a pending proposal.

candidate_claims.note: True of turns 4–7, but presented as the whole session, omitting three other goals.
'Natural language processing' has no basis; omits Claude Code internals, macOS/zsh, and benchmarking/cost economics.
candidate_claims.reason: Most listed domains are genuinely present; 'natural language processing' is an unsupported addition to an otherwise real list.

candidate_claims.note: The routing baseline was already executed (4 headless cells, $1.72, ~2.7s median choose time); it ran against SPINE in clean cells, not 'a set of local transcripts'.
candidate_claims.reason: The routing baseline is a real event, but it was already executed and ran against SPINE in clean cells, not pending against local transcripts.
